rails_8_1_upgrade_guide_and_release_note.upgrade_guide_8_0_to_8_1: guides.rubyonrails.org 'Upgrading from Rails 8.0 to Rails 8.1' (read 2026-10-25) has a single subsection, 2.1 'The table columns inside schema.rb are now sorted alphabetically', plus a pointer to the 8.1 release notes. It does not mention order-dependent finders, mb_chars, ActiveSupport::Configurable or to_time_preserves_timezone — those are release-notes deprecations, not guide items. The plan's wording ('the upgrade guide lists ... deprecations worth fixing now') conflated the two

release_notes_deprecations_vs_this_app.order_dependent_finders: Active Record: 'Deprecate using an order dependent finder method (e.g. #first) without an order'. activerecord 8.1.4 finder_methods.rb#ordered_relation warns (or raises, under raise_on_missing_required_finder_order_columns) ONLY when the relation has no order AND the model has no implicit_order_column, query_constraints or primary_key to fall back on. Every model here has an id primary key, so `.first` still orders by id and never warns — the suite emitted no such deprecation. The two relation sites were given order(:created_at) anyway (see finder_ordering); the two Array#first sites are unaffected
release_notes_deprecations_vs_this_app.to_time_preserves_timezone: Active Support: 'Remove deprecated support for to_time to preserve the system local time' and 'Deprecate config.active_support.to_time_preserves_timezone'. activesupport 8.1.4 active_support.rb: both the reader and the writer warn '`config.active_support.to_time_preserves_timezone` is deprecated and will be removed in Rails 8.2'; TimeWithZone#to_time is now unconditionally getlocal(time_zone). So the plan's 'set :zone explicitly to silence the deprecation' would CREATE a deprecation in 8.1; the key is not set anywhere (the probe confirms `config.active_support.key?(:to_time_preserves_timezone)` → false) and the four boot warnings are gone
release_notes_deprecations_vs_this_app.mb_chars: Active Support: 'Deprecate String#mb_chars and ActiveSupport::Multibyte::Chars' — grep app/ config/ lib/ spec/: no hits
release_notes_deprecations_vs_this_app.active_support_configurable: Active Support: 'Deprecate ActiveSupport::Configurable' — no hits in app/ config/ lib/ spec/; omniauth-rails_csrf_protection 2.0.1 (Phase 8) already dropped it; no such warning in the suite's stderr
release_notes_deprecations_vs_this_app.insert_all_upsert_all_update_all: no hits in app/ or lib/
release_notes_deprecations_vs_this_app.benchmark_ms_time_since: no Benchmark or Time#since(Time) use — no hits
release_notes_deprecations_vs_this_app.active_job_enqueue_after_transaction_com: removed in 8.1; never set here (Phase 15 recorded that 8.0 had already dropped it from the 7.2 block)
release_notes_deprecations_vs_this_app.action_pack_removals: semicolon query-string separators, leading-bracket skipping and multi-path routes: none used (routes.rb has one path per route; the smoke and request specs exercise the real query strings)

It does NOT set active_support.to_time_preserves_timezone = :zone any more — the 8.0.5.1 defaults file listed three keys, the 8.1.4 block has two, because 8.1 removed the old to_time behaviour and deprecated the setting. effects_here.strict_freshness_true: ActionDispatch::Http::Cache::Request.strict_freshness true (probe): when a client sends both If-None-Match and If-Modified-Since only the ETag is considered (RFC 7232 §6). No fresh_when / stale? / etag / expires_in use anywhere in app/ (grep), so no controller emits ETag/Last-Modified conditional-GET responses — the only HTTP-level effect is on Rack::ETag-generated ETags for the HTML pages, where no Last-Modified header is ever set, so behaviour is identical. No status code or header change in the request/feature specs
effects_here.regexp_timeout_1: Regexp.timeout 1.0 (probe; was nil under load_defaults 7.2). Process-global: every Regexp without its own timeout now raises Regexp::TimeoutError after 1 s of matching. app/ and lib/ contain no regexp code (the only patterns in config/ are commented-out initializer examples); the regexps that run per request belong to Rails routing, Devise's email validator (Devise.email_regexp, linear), Rack and the sanitizer — all bounded, none anywhere near 1 s on the inputs this app accepts (the API's largest payload is a scenario with nested solutions; parameters are numeric). Suite green with it in force
effects_here.to_time_preserves_timezone: no longer part of the block (see railties_8_1_4_block) — nothing to flip; the four boot deprecations Phase 15 recorded are absent in every run (see warnings_observed)

load_defaults.yjit: unchanged from Phase 15: load_defaults 7.2's `yjit = true` still applies in every environment (probe: RubyVM::YJIT.enabled? true in production mode; the suite ran with YJIT on). load_defaults 8.1 (Phase 20) changes this to `yjit = !Rails.env.local?`, i.e. production only

finder_ordering.decision: app/controllers/application_controller.rb#first_sign_in_scenario and app/controllers/users/registrations_controller.rb#after_sign_up_path_for: `automation_scenarios.first` → `automation_scenarios.order(:created_at).first`. OPTIONAL under 8.1 (see release_notes_deprecations_vs_this_app.order_dependent_finders — AutomationScenario has a primary key, so the implicit `ORDER BY id` continues and no deprecation fires, now or in 8.2). Kept as a clarification of intent ('the owner's first scenario by creation') since the plan called for it and it costs nothing
finder_ordering.sql: SELECT "automation_scenarios".* FROM "automation_scenarios" WHERE owner_id = ? AND owner_type = 'User' ORDER BY "automation_scenarios"."created_at" ASC LIMIT 1 (probe); before: ORDER BY id ASC LIMIT 1
finder_ordering.spec_safety: User#after_create creates exactly one scenario (app/models/user.rb), so for every user in the specs both orderings return the same single record. spec/requests/user_sessions_spec.rb:26 and spec/controllers/application_controller_spec.rb:10 compute the expected redirect with `user.automation_scenarios.first` (primary-key order) and still pass; no spec was changed. created_at is a timestamp(6) column, so even with several scenarios the order is well defined
finder_ordering.left_alone: app/services/jwt_token_service.rb:14 (`.first` on an Array from a chain) and app/services/solution_pair.rb:52 (`point.first` on a two-element Array) — not Active Record relations
